title.value: Fine-tuning Reinforcement Learning Models is Secretly a Forgetting Mitigation Problem
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the document as well as at the top of each page.
title.quote: Fine-tuning Reinforcement Learning Models is Secretly a Forgetting Mitigation Problem

analysis.description: This paper investigates the challenges of fine-tuning pre-trained reinforcement learning (RL) models, focusing on the problem of forgetting pre-trained capabilities. It identifies two main issues: state coverage gap and imperfect cloning gap, which can occur during the fine-tuning process. The study empirically demonstrates the severity of this problem across various environments and proposes knowledge retention techniques as a solution to leverage full capabilities of pre-trained models. Techniques like behavioral cloning, kickstarting, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), and episodic memory are explored.

type.justification: The paper conducts empirical studies to demonstrate the issue of forgetting in reinforcement learning and tests various solutions to mitigate it, such as knowledge retention techniques across multiple environments.
type.quote: Through a detailed empirical analysis of the challenging NetHack and Montezuma’s Revenge environments, we show that standard knowledge retention techniques mitigate the problem.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on fine-tuning models within the context of reinforcement learning (RL), addressing the specific challenges faced in RL scenarios.
name.quote: However, fine-tuning reinforcement learning (RL) models remains a challenge.

name.justification: The paper discusses various techniques such as behavioral cloning, kickstarting, and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), all related to retaining knowledge in pre-trained RL models during fine-tuning.
name.quote: Finally, we show that phrasing state coverage gap and imperfect cloning gap as instances of forgetting is meaningful as typical retention techniques...can alleviate these problems.

name.justification: The paper addresses the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in RL, where the model loses pre-trained capabilities during fine-tuning, which necessitates the use of retention techniques.
name.quote: As such, the main recommendation of our work is that methods targeting catastrophic forgetting should be routinely used in transfer RL scenarios.

name.justification: The study explores how pre-trained models can be fine-tuned for new tasks, which is a central topic in transfer learning within the domain of reinforcement learning.
name.quote: ...fine-tuning neural networks is a widespread technique in deep learning for knowledge transfer between datasets.

name.justification: The environments used and the modifications suggested involve the architecture of neural networks for enabling better retention of pre-trained knowledge.
name.quote: It was trained using behavioral cloning on 115B environment transitions sampled from AutoAscend, a rule-based agent that is currently the best-performing bot.
